name: Chili (food medium)
description: Food-derived medium: metabolizable components of Chili [Dishes] from FooDB, plus a standard M9 mineral base. Organic components use presence-based uptake bounds; FooDB content retained. Measured compounds with no BiGG exchange are listed under uncovered.

provenance.citation: FooDB v2020-04-07 (Wishart DS et al., foodb.ca). Content sources: USDA.
provenance.notes: Organic components mapped from FooDB compounds to BiGG via InChIKey/name. Mineral base added. Bounds presence-based; foodb_content retained. Unmapped measured compounds kept in uncovered (v2 completeness fix). IMPORTANT: composition values are taken from the archived FooDB 2020-04-07 CSV data release; FooDB's live food page no longer displays this bulk composition, so it will appear empty. Verify individual compounds via the per-component cross-reference links. Underlying content was aggregated by FooDB from USDA / DTU / Phenol Explorer.
provenance.verification: expert-curated (multi-source food composition; growth-relevant profile completed, FooDB noise removed)
curation_sources: USDA SR Legacy NDB 22904 'Chili con carne with beans, canned entree' (247 kcal per 242 g cup) — full proximate/mineral/vitamin/fatty-acid/sugar panel, rescaled to per 100 g
FooDB FOOD00707 (identity: prepared dish 'Chili' = chili con carne, food group Dishes/Tex-Mex)
USDA FoodData Central (fdc.nal.usda.gov) mirror of NDB 22904
provenance.curation_notes: Dominant carbon/energy sources are STARCH (6.9 g/100g, from beans) plus free sugars (sucrose>fructose>glucose, ~1.9 g/100g total from tomato/onion); substantial mixed beef+bean protein (5.8 g/100g) supplies amino-acid N. This is a MEAT-containing dish, so cholesterol, B12, and animal-type saturated/trans fatty acids are genuine, not FooDB plant-food noise. curation_added: Individual free sugars with amounts: sucrose 1.03, D-fructose 0.49, D-glucose 0.34 g/100g
Starch quantified (6.90 g/100g) — the dominant fermentable carbohydrate
citric acid + malic acid (organic acids from tomato, growth-relevant carbon; present, flagged for quantification)
Full mineral amounts (Na, K, P, Ca, Mg, Fe, Zn, Mn, Cu, Se)
Full B-vitamin amounts + choline, vitamin K, vitamin E, folate, B12
L-valine and L-phenylalanine (proteinogenic amino acids absent from the current list)

curation_removed.name: Genistein
curation_removed.reason: Soy-specific isoflavone. Chili con carne uses kidney beans (Phaseolus vulgaris), not soy; genistein is not a characteristic measured constituent of this dish. FooDB generic-legume prediction, unquantified.

curation_removed.name: Glycitein
curation_removed.reason: Soy-specific isoflavone; same rationale as genistein. Not characteristic of a kidney-bean/beef dish; FooDB predicted, not measured.

curation_removed.name: Isoflavones (generic)
curation_removed.reason: Umbrella phytoestrogen class carried over from soy; not a defining or measured nutrient of chili con carne. FooDB noise.

curation_removed.name: Gamolenic acid (GLA, 18:3 n-6)
curation_removed.reason: USDA SR 22904 measures gamma-linolenic acid at 0.00 g; GLA is essentially absent from beef/kidney-bean/tomato fat. FooDB artifact.

curation_removed.name: Nickel
curation_removed.reason: Ultratrace element at contaminant/non-nutritional level; not quantified as a growth nutrient here. FooDB trace listing.

coverage_source.definition: pct_covered_all = components / (components + unresolved ingredients) — the legacy metric, which counts pipeline-derived components as covered. pct_covered_source = source-stated components / (those + unresolved ingredients + ingredients replaced by derived components). Component classes come from tools/component_evidence_classes.tsv. A null value means the denominator was zero; it does not mean 100.
